name: Marcus Aurelius
deathplace: on campaign in Pannonia, at Vindobona (Vienna) or near Sirmium
knownFor: The last of the Five Good Emperors, and the Stoic who wrote the Meditations for himself.

works.title: Meditations
works.note: twelve books in Greek, written on campaign as a source of guidance for himself

events.text: Adopted by Antoninus Pius, who had himself just been adopted as Hadrian's heir, and so became heir to the throne in turn.
Married Faustina, the daughter of Antoninus Pius.
Became emperor on Antoninus's death, sharing the throne with his adoptive brother Lucius Verus.
The Antonine Plague began, in or about this year, and devastated the population of the empire.
Named his son Commodus Caesar; the Marcomannic Wars on the Danube frontier took up most of the rest of his reign.
Died at 58 in his military quarters on the Danube frontier; Commodus succeeded him.

relevance: The Meditations were never meant for readers: they are a Stoic's private notes on duty, impermanence and self-command, set down during years of war. They remain among the most widely read works of ancient philosophy.
influence: His reign closed the age of the Five Good Emperors and the Pax Romana, and his column and equestrian statue still stand in Rome. As a philosopher he is remembered through a book he did not publish.
